newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU possible without hitting 3.0 pct - German SPD.
newsitem.headline: EMU possible without hitting 3.0 pct - German SPD.

text.p: European economic and monetary union (EMU) could begin even if participating countries' budget deficits exceed the target of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, German opposition parties said on Monday.
Economically, it did not matter if the deficit was 2.9 or 3.1 percent, Social Democrat parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping told journalists.
Joschka Fischer, parliamentary speaker for the Greens party, said the Maastricht Treaty did not specify a ratio of 3.0 percent.
The Finance Minister had set a trap for himself by insisting on strict adherence to the 3.0 percent "reference value" as if it were a treaty obligation, Fischer said.
The more important factor was sustainable adherence to the criteria, which have already been met for inflation, interest rates and exchange rate stability, Fischer said.
Fischer also said he supported a large EMU launch. Italy, Spain and Portugal have made considerable efforts to be able to participate.
